reviews.review:
Unique, yet enjoyable :) 
Not Bad, Anyone who loves stunt action + shooting must play!

The short version of this review is that while I personally found the game fun to play, I can't really recommend it over the long term. I only realized that after putting 400+ hours and a total of $90 of microtransactions ($20 option * 6 times w/ 20% off coupons) into this game. My reasons are outlined below:

PROS:

-Fun either solo or multiplayer (but then again everything is fun with multiplayer)

-Updated reguarly with hotfixes and content

-Platinum (the virtual currency in this game) can be traded, meaning you don't have to spend a single cent if you're willing to farm rare stuff and trade them in exchange, but this requires much patience, espeically when you're new

-Various mission types

-Various random events (when you're part of a syndicate, for example) can be pretty tense when you're new

-Each Warframe has a different gameplay style

-Everything can be acquired via in-game credits with the exception of some cosmetic items

CONS:

-"Stealth" aspect of the game is substandard. Almost doesn't matter aside from Spy missions, stealth is not appreciated nor viable

-You are forced to buy inventory slots for weapons and new Warframes to experience more content, which requires Platinum

-Weapons and Warframes can only reach their full potential via special items (what the community calls "potatoes") which cannot be obtained normally. You can only buy them on demand with Platinum or wait for an alert mission that offers it as a reward, which happens very rarely. It's also a very rare daily login reward, but good luck with that. They're needed to expand mod capacity while the other special item (called "Forma") are required to half the cost of installing mods on your equipment, which is critical to being powerful, but fortunately the latter is fairly easy to obtain.

-The market makes absolutely no sense. Aside from the ridiculous Platinum cost of everything in general, an example is a rare resource called "Orokin cell". The market provides a permanent blueprint to craft them as an alternative to farming them on a mid-game world, but the cost is laughably ridiculous and much harder to do than just farming them.

-Platinum is way too expensive to purchase directly from the market, even with discounts. The discount coupons can be obtained as daily login rewards. Generally not advised to buy any amount of Platinum from the market without these, even if the savings is small. That is, if you must buy virtual currency.

-No votekick/ban function

-Archwing missions are boring and pointless

-RNG based rewards, essentially turns the game into a giant grindfest and a waste of time when you don't get what you want. This is 90% of the time.

-Gameplay gets very grindy and repetitive after a while, especially if your arsenal is limited. Also, It's all just about numbers going up, especially at end game. Not much strategy when you're one shotting everything with six or seven figures in Tower 4 void missions.

-Speaking of endgame content (or lack thereof), every mission pretty much becomes a laborous, linear chore when all you have left to do is farm resources, credits, or prime parts to feed mastery rank or whatever.

-Numerous game breaking glitches despite regular hotfixes

-Questionable physics. Parkour 2.0 has gotten me stuck in terrain more than once, even still today

-Lag can be crippling

-Balance issues. For example, leveling up equipment is really unbalanced (Draco anyone?)

-Too many experienced players asking for "taxis" to planets they don't even bother to unlock themselves

-Sometimes facepalm community that doesn't seem to get better. Refer to previous point. Also keyshare ditchers.

-Transmutation of mods is a complete waste of credits and time

-This game requires a ton of patience if you're not willing to spend a single cent. It's not pay2win, but it is very pay2advance. New players have it extremely rough.

-Crafting almost everything that matters in this game takes at least 12 hours in real time. They are mostly weapons. Forma take twice as long for every one. And you need lots of them. Warframes take six times longer. They can be rushed to immediate completion with Platinum, but nothing in this game is worth rushing.

-Mastery rank becomes mostly irrelevant after unlocking everything. The only reason to use bad weapons is to feed MR. These weapons are called "mastery fodder"

-Useless resources (Alloy Plates and faction resources like Detonite Injectors) that just pile up in your inventory and overly rare resources (Neurodes, Neural Sensors) that require hours of farming for a handful of them.

-Ordis (The mainframe and steward of your ship). Ceaselessly annoying and there's no way to mute him.

I have not tried PvP yet, but it exists. So again, even though I personally find the game fun and somewhat addicting, I can't really recommend it upon closer consideration. I do think it's worth a play since it's free. And I think it's one of the better free to play games out there. To this game's credit, it made me want to spend money on it, which I only exceptionally do with free to play games. And this is the first free to play game that made me want to spend as much as I did because I was having that much fun. The only reason I spent that much is because I was curious whether I really liked this or not, and I have a lot of Platinum to keep me going for a while as more updates and content roll out to determine that.

Another review described this game as a grindy Korean MMO. That's pretty much what the game feels like.
